# Lab 25.13: Trigger, Investigate & Remediate a Finding

## What We Are Going to Do
Create a risky setting on purpose, watch Security Command Center find it, investigate it, fix it, and see the finding close.

## Steps

1. **Create a misconfiguration.** Use a test project with no public access prevention policy.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage buckets create gs://$PROJECT_ID-public-test --location=us-central1 --uniform-bucket-level-access
gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://$PROJECT_ID-public-test \
  --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer

gcloud compute firewall-rules create open-ssh-test --network=default \
  --allow=tcp:22 --source-ranges=0.0.0.0/0</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Wait for the findings.** Security Health Analytics scans changes in near real time for many detectors. Look for `PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL` and `OPEN_SSH_PORT` in **Findings**.

3. **Investigate.** Open the `PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL` finding. Read:
   - **Resource**: the bucket
   - **Severity** and, in Premium, **Attack exposure score**
   - **Next steps**: how to fix it
   - **Source properties**: the exact problem

4. **Find who did it.** In **Logs Explorer**:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • TEXT
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">protoPayload.methodName="storage.setIamPermissions"
protoPayload.resourceName:"public-test"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Remediate.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage buckets remove-iam-policy-binding gs://$PROJECT_ID-public-test \
  --member=allUsers --role=roles/storage.objectViewer
gcloud compute firewall-rules delete open-ssh-test --quiet</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


6. **Confirm.** After the next scan, both findings change to **Inactive**.

7. **Optional, Premium.** Event Threat Detection test: grant a role on a test project to a personal Gmail account. A `Persistence: IAM Anomalous Grant` threat finding appears. Remove the grant right away.

8. **Clean up.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage rm --recursive gs://$PROJECT_ID-public-test</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Public bucket | `PUBLIC_BUCKET_ACL` finding |
| Open SSH | `OPEN_SSH_PORT` finding |
| Investigation | Finding details plus audit logs |
| After fix | Finding becomes Inactive |
